Article Title: 7 killed, several injured in stampede-like incident at Bihar's Lakhisarai temple
Article Text:
A stampede-like situation in Bihar temple, claims several lives.

Earlier incident in Muzaffarpur

NEW DELHI: Seven people were killed and several others injured in a stampede-like incident at Ashokdham Temple in Bihar’s Lakhisarai on early Monday, as news agency ANI quoted Bihar police.The incident took place as a large crowd had gathered at the temple, officials said.It also took place on Shravan’s Somvaar, a day that typically draws large numbers of devotees to Shiva temples.SDPO Shivam Kumar told ANI, "Seven casualties have been reported. It is being said that an electric pole fell there and people were electrocuted, which led to a stampede-like situation. We can tell you the exact reason only after verifying everything."Lakhisarai DM Shailendra Kumar said, "The crowd swelled in an unprecedented manner. Around 6.30-6.45 am, two trains came here that too added to the crowd. Arrangements were made as we had anticipated the crowd."Explaining how the incident unfolded, the DM said the sheer pressure of the crowd caused one side of the barricading to give way.“We then came to know that the barricading broke on one side due to the crowd, and people fell on each other.We rushed 10-15 people here immediately,” he added.The injured were shifted to local medical facilities for treatment. District administration officials and police personnel remained at the site to manage the crowd and prevent any further untoward incident.Further investigation into the incident is underway, with more details awaited.In a separate incident on August 12, a passenger bus travelling from Motihari towards Chhatarpur caught fire on the NH-27 Barji overbridge in Muzaffarpur around 12.45 am.Sub-Divisional Fire Officer of Motipur Amrita Kumari said the fire was caused by a short circuit. All 35 passengers were safely evacuated.
Article Summary: Stampede-like incident took place at Ashokdham Temple in Bihar's Lakhisarai. Incident took place on Shravan’s Somvaar, a day that typically draws large numbers of devotees to Shiva temples. It is being said that an electric pole fell there and people were electrocuted.

Article Title: Slugfest over Congress's P Chidambaram's 'dimagi Naxal' post
Article Text:
Kiren Rijiju said PM was not referring to the opposition after P Chidambaram's 'dimagi Naxal' post.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: PM Modi's 'dimagi Naxal' remark on August 15 became the subject of a political slugfest Sunday, with Congress 's P Chidambaram saying he was "proud to be a dimagi Naxal" to which BJP replied that the ex-home minister's remark shows how UPA govt was run.Union minister Kiren Rijiju said the PM was not referring to the opposition. "Only following are Dimagi Naxals: 1. Who support Maoists and reject Indian Constitution. 2. Who stand with separatists & support Article 370. 4. Who want to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India," he said on X. tnnCongress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera responded on X: "Brother Kiren Rijiju, get your counting right first, then we'll answer. After 1 and 2 comes 3, not 4."BJP ally TDP MP and former IPS officer Tenneti Krishna Prasad backed PM's "dimagi Naxals" remarks, saying a new form of "intellectual Naxalism" has emerged. "The forest Naxalites and Maoists have been removed from forests; now this new form has emerged. Therefore, we have to remain extremely vigilant and protect our country, especially our youth," he said in a video statement, according to news agency PTI.In an apparent reference to Rahul Gandhi, Tenneti Krishna said, "Today, forest Naxalites have gone, and a new form has emerged. I call them 'intellectual Naxalites'. They do not operate in forests; they operate in cities. They organise seminars in air-conditioned halls.BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad said Chidambaram "has become the face of the Congress ecosystem which nurtures Maoism". He recalled that as home minister, Chidambaram had expressed willingness to hold talks with Naxals when they had killed 76 security personnel, while JNU had witnessed an event lauding the killers. Under Modi govt, Maoism has not only been finished off but national flag is also flying in former strongholds of Maoists, he said.BJP also kept up its attack on Congress for allegedly insulting national song Vande Mataram, with BJP president Nitin Nabin, saying bowing to fundamentalist forces has become a permanent policy of Congress. Besides the attempt by Sonia Gandhi to "stop" the recital of Vande Mataram's full version at Congress headquarters, its govt in Kerala removed the song altogether from the Independence Day event, he said.
Article Summary: P Chidambaram said he was "proud to be a dimagi Naxal" to which BJP replied that the remark shows how UPA govt was run. Union minister Kiren Rijiju said the PM was not referring to the opposition. Bowing to fundamentalist forces has become a permanent policy of Congress.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi's 'chhatron ki goonj' rally in Pune will be exclusively for girls
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi said the upcoming rally in Pune on Aug 22 will be exclusively for girls.

NEW DELHI: As part of his "chhatron ki goonj" meetings targeting the youth, Congress's Rahul Gandhi said the upcoming rally in Pune on Aug 22 will be exclusively for girls.The announcement came along with Rahul's social media video post featuring an interaction with some Jantar Mantar protesters. Rahul said, "The courage with which India's youngsters have stood firm against PM Modi's violent regime, demanding accountability, is commendable. " He added, "I am proud of every single young person - especially the girls who faced the BJP goons' misbehaviour, verbal abuse and violence, even being forced to apologise to the Prime Minister."Announcing the Pune meeting, Rahul said, "But now their (girls') voices cannot be silenced. On Aug 22, Chhatron ki goonj is arriving in Pune-and this time, the event will be exclusively for girls. Now the girls will speak, and the country will listen." TNN
Article Summary: The announcement came along with Rahul's social media video post featuring an interaction with some Jantar Mantar protesters. Rahul said, "The courage with which India's youngsters have stood firm against PM Modi's violent regime, demanding accountability, is commendable"

Article Title: Harsimrat Kaur Badal 'deeply touched' by PM Modi's 'kind gesture' after attack on Sukhbir Badal
Article Text:
Sukhbir Badal was attacked at a gurudwara in Maharashtra's Nanded

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal on Friday said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief, Sukhbir Singh Badal , who was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.This marked the Badal family's first reaction to the attack on the former Punjab deputy chief minister."Truly grateful, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, for your personal call to inquire about Sardar Sukhbir Singh Badal ji’s health and for your good wishes for his speedy recovery following the dastardly attack on him inside a Gurudwara Sahib in Nanded, Maharashtra," Harsimrat Badal, SAD's only Lok Sabha MP, wrote on X.She also thanked the prime minister for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with the state police in the probe."Your concern, support and wishes during this difficult time mean a lot to all of us in the family, our party and to the people of Punjab. I am deeply touched by your kind gesture. I am also grateful to you for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with Maharashtra Police in the probe," the Bathinda MP added.On Thursday, Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked by a kirpan-wielding assailant while leaving the Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara at Mudkhed in Maharashtra’s Nanded district. The assailant was arrested at the spot.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered an inquiry into the attack and spoke to Sukhbir Singh Badal over the phone. The SAD president is learnt to have told Fadnavis that he was stable, ANI reported.Earlier, Badal was also targeted in an attempted shooting at the Golden Temple in Amritsar in December 2024 while he was performing “seva”. The attacker allegedly tried to fire at him but was overpowered before he could cause any harm.The 2024 attack took place while Badal was carrying out “seva” after the Akal Takht, the highest temporal authority in Sikhism, declared him a “tankhaiya,” or guilty of religious misconduct, over decisions taken by the SAD-led Punjab government between 2007 and 2017.The SAD and BJP, which currently lead the governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, are former allies. In 2020, the SAD ended its alliance with the BJP in protest against the Centre’s contentious farm laws, which were later withdrawn.Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week, triggering speculation that the former allies could reunite ahead of the Punjab assembly elections early next year.
Article Summary: Harsimrat Kaur Badal said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief. Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.

Article Title: Bankim Chandra's kin Sumitro Chatterjee writes to Sonia Gandhi, seeks apology
Article Text:
The controversy erupted after a video from Congress's Aug 15 function showed Sonia gesturing and speaking to party president Kharge.

NEW DELHI: The row over the full rendition of Vande Mataram at Congress headquarters on Independence Day acquired a Bankim Chandra connection, with BJP MLA Sumitro Chatterjee, a direct descendant of the national song's author, writing to Sonia Gandhi Saturday and demanding an unconditional apology to the country.The controversy erupted after a video from Congress's Aug 15 function showed Sonia gesturing and speaking to party president Mallikarjun Kharge while the full version of Vande Mataram was being sung.In his letter, Chatterjee said the episode had left him with "deep pain, emptiness and anguish", alleging Sonia's "physical gestures" reflected "unease, impatience and repeated attempts to stop" the song. He said the reaction hurt him not only as a citizen but as a direct descendant of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. TNN
Article Summary: BJP MLA Sumitro Chatterjee, a direct descendant of the national song's author, writes to Sonia Gandhi. He demands an unconditional apology to the country. The controversy erupted after a video from Congress's Aug 15 function showed Sonia gesturing and speaking to party president Kharge.

Article Title: NTA admits errors, orders fresh NET for 3 subjects
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: National Testing Agency (NTA) on Sunday acknowledged that the UGC-NET papers in English, Commerce and Sociology had multiple errors and repeated questions, and said the defects were too extensive to be addressed simply by dropping questions after the answer-key challenge process. It has ordered fresh examinations for all three subjects.The re-tests will be held on September 9 and 10. English will be conducted from 9am to noon on September 9, Commerce from 3pm to 6pm the same day, and Sociology from 9am to noon on September 10. No additional examination fee will be charged.The decision came hours after NTA released provisional answer keys for 84 of the 87 UGC-NET subjects but withheld the keys for these three papers, nearly seven weeks after the June examination.NTA said a committee set up after receiving “several complaints” found “many factual, typographical, translation errors”, including misspelt names of prominent scholars, garbled book titles, wrongly worded questions, grammatical and punctuation mistakes and non-standard terms used for established concepts. The committee also found repetition of a “significant number” of questions previously asked.The agency said papers carrying defects of this extent did not meet the standards of a fair and error-free examination and that the problems could not be corrected merely by dropping questions after challenges were received.TOI had on July 1 reported complaints over the Sociology and English papers. Sociology candidates alleged that the June 30 paper contained spelling and grammatical errors, mangled names of well-known thinkers, poor Hindi translations and questions apparently unrelated to the prescribed syllabus. Some also alleged that parts of the paper appeared AI-generated.Candidates had pointed out that “Ritzer” appeared as “Putzer”, “Parsons” as “Parsow”, “Ghurye” as “Ghunye” and A R Desai as “A K Desai”, among several other errors.The English paper had also come under scrutiny after candidates alleged that 67 of its 150 questions were identical to questions asked in the 2024 examination, with even the sequence of answer options reportedly unchanged. Complaints over repetition were subsequently raised in Commerce as well.The episode comes two years after the June 2024 UGC-NET was cancelled a day after it was held following inputs received by UGC from the National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit under the home ministry indicating that the integrity of the examination may have been compromised. The test was subsequently conducted afresh.The current re-examination will, however, not hold up results in the other 84 subjects. NTA said their results would be declared as scheduled and JRF allocation and certificates for Assistant Professor and PhD eligibility would not be delayed.For assistant professor eligibility, NTA said the number qualifying would be 6% of candidates who appeared in the June test or the re-test, whichever is higher.
Article Summary: National Testing Agency says papers in English, Commerce and Sociology had multiple errors and repeated questions. NTA says defects were too extensive to be addressed simply by dropping questions after the answer-key challenge process. It has ordered fresh examinations for all three subjects on September 9 and 10.

Article Title: 'Remove bulletproof glass or I won't speak': Ex-officer recalls PM Modi's demand on I-Day 2014
Article Text:
PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," the officer recalled.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort before delivering his first Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014.Speaking about the episode, Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15. The officials had specifically discussed the bulletproof glass barrier placed in front of the Prime Minister."Me and the Director of Intelligence Bureau (IB), went to PM Modi for a briefing before August 15 because it was his first Independence Day where he would address the country from the ramparts of the Red Fort (as the Prime Minister).""During that conversation we explained him (PM Modi) that there is a barrier in front of him which is the bulletproof glass. PM Modi said, 'if this stays in front of me, I would not be able to address the citizens'," he told news agency IANS.Mathur said security officials initially opposed removing the shield because of the risks involved. The location offers a wide view of the surrounding area, including buildings in Chandni Chowk, making security arrangements particularly sensitive."From our side, this was naturally a security issue. As people know, the entire Chandni Chowk area is visible from there (Red Fort) where there are many buildings. That is why, from a security standpoint we urged the Prime Minister to rethink his decision. However, PM Modi clearly stated that if this (bulletproof shield) is not removed, he will not address."The former defence secretary said the security team eventually agreed to Modi's demand and removed the glass barrier just hours before the Independence Day ceremony."Due to this, I and the director of IB changed our standpoint and decided to remove the bulletproof glass. This glass shield was then removed on the intervening night of August 14 and 15, at about 2 am," Mathur added.The episode was recalled as Modi once again departed from established security protocol during the 80th Independence Day celebrations on Saturday, when he met schoolchildren, NCC cadets and 'My Bharat' volunteers at the Red Fort after his address.During the interaction, a young girl approached Modi and bent down to touch his feet. As she did so, her cap slipped from her head and fell to the ground.Modi immediately bent down, picked up the cap and placed it back on the girl's head. The gesture drew smiles and applause from the children and people around them.
Article Summary: Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort. Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15.

Article Title: Parliament at a standstill, protests on streets: The Monsoon session story
Article Text:
19% in Lok Sabha, 39% in Rajya Sabha: How Monsoon Session unfolded beyond the Parliament

Parliament sees low productivity

'Not a good session in terms of discussion'

Bills passed in Parliament

Bills passed by both the Houses

Bills passed in this Monsoon Session

The session began with a protest

From Pradhan to Shah

Rahul Gandhi trains guns at Amit Shah

The debate that moved between the House and outside

Monsoon Session

Jharkhand adds another layer

Pradhan calls Rahul Gandhi a 'habitual liar'

Then came the Ram Mandir protest

A Parliament that worked, but talked less

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For 25 days, Parliament’s Monsoon Session played out on two different stages.Inside the Houses, proceedings were repeatedly disrupted, adjournments were frequent and Question Hour had barely any time remaining. Outside, political activity rarely stopped. Students marched, opposition leaders protested, ministers traded charges, and the Parliament complex itself became a stage for demonstrations and symbolic political performances.Held from July 20 to August 13, the session produced an unusual contrast: legislation moved forward, but much of the political confrontation surrounding it played out beyond the floor of the two Houses.The numbers underline that contrast. Lok Sabha functioned for approximately 19% of its scheduled time, while Rajya Sabha functioned for around 39%. Question Hour was particularly badly hit, with less than 1% of its scheduled time utilised. The session had 19 sittings spread over 25 days.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju acknowledged the distinction between legislative output and debate.“It was a good session…we have passed 13 bills; but it was not a good session in terms of discussion,” he said, while accusing the opposition of avoiding debate despite the government's willingness to discuss issues.Yet government business did move, much of it through voice votes amid opposition sloganeering.Eleven Bills were introduced in Lok Sabha and two in Rajya Sabha. Twelve Bills were passed by Lok Sabha and 12 by Rajya Sabha, with 12 Bills cleared by both Houses during the session.Two Bills replacing and incorporating the provisions of ordinances issued before the session, the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 and the Income-Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, were also passed by both Houses.The Demands for Excess Grants for 2022-23 were taken up, with the related Appropriation Bill passed by Lok Sabha on August 4 and returned by Rajya Sabha on August 6. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was referred to a Joint Committee for examination.Among the more politically significant measures was the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced amid concerns over public examinations and paper leaks.The Bill came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced stringent measures to prevent such incidents in the future, including multiple selfie videos directly addressing students.It provides for speedy investigations and time-bound trials, with investigations to be completed within two months and trials within three months. It also provides for Special Fast Track Courts and Special Public Prosecutors, allows the Centre to constitute Special Task Forces where necessary, enhances penalties and creates a time-bound appellate mechanism before a Division Bench of the High Court.The Bill was passed by both Houses and received presidential assent.Its debate also offered a glimpse of how political parties were trying to speak directly to younger voters. BJP’s younger leaders took the lead in explaining the legislation and the Centre’s position, while the opposition made its own pitch. Both sides adopted Gen Z vocabulary, trading barbs with phrases such as “clock it”, “FOMO” and “delulu”.Other major Bills passed during the session included the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, which seeks to bring Vande Mataram within the ambit of the 1971 Act; the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, which proposes stricter procedures for delayed registration; and the MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, which provides for a national digital platform for voluntary registration and seeks to improve access to finance and resolve delayed-payment disputes faster.The Bankers' Books Evidence Bill expands the definition of bankers' books to cover physical, electronic, digital, virtual and cloud-based records. The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill proposes changing the state’s name from Kerala to Keralam. Other legislation dealt with cooperative development, tribunals and the mining sector.But these measures were not what defined the political atmosphere of the session. That distinction belonged to the protests outside.The Monsoon Session opened against the backdrop of a large student mobilisation at Jantar Mantar over NEET examination irregularities.The protest had been building for weeks. Scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk had been on a hunger strike for more than 20 days when the Centre intervened and removed him from the protest site.His removal intensified the agitation, with students going ahead with their scheduled “Sansad gherao”. Security personnel, including the Rapid Action Force and Delhi Police, were deployed as the protesters marched towards Parliament.The distance was less than 1.5 km, but the march quickly turned into a major confrontation.Pellet guns, lathi-charge and tear gas were used, with more than 60 people injured and admitted to nearby Lady Hardinge Medical College and Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.The police action immediately became a political issue, with opposition leaders turning their focus towards Union home minister Amit Shah because the security forces involved came under the home ministry’s jurisdiction.The student protests subsequently spread beyond Delhi. The pressure group Cockroach Janta Party’s delegation met PM Modi-led cabinet ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh, after which the situation moved towards normalcy.One of the protesters’ major demands was the removal of Dharmendra Pradhan as education minister.On July 25, Pradhan resigned from the post, making his departure one of the defining political developments of the session.Pradhan’s resignation did not end the political confrontation.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi had not joined the initial Jantar Mantar protest but emerged as a prominent voice in the political battle that followed. His focus shifted from Pradhan to Shah, whom he repeatedly attacked over the police crackdown on students on July 20.“As home minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did? Are the people in plainclothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Youth and students, future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability,” Rahul said.He argued that Shah either directly ordered the use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas, making him “culpable” for the treatment of the protesters, or did not know what the police were doing, making him “incompetent”.“In either case, he has to go,” Rahul said, calling on Prime Minister Narendra Modi to sack the home minister.Rahul also alleged that students were facing threats, including through face recognition and Bajrang Dal. “These are our children and the govt has no business threatening them or beating them. They have not committed any crime. They should not be punished,” he said.He later made the demand for Shah’s removal explicit, saying: “Shah is responsible and we are not going to let him get away with it.”At the AICC headquarters, with Shah’s photograph displayed on a large screen, Rahul accused the home minister of being responsible for the treatment of students and criticised his absence from Lok Sabha, saying it showed that he was “guilty”.Inside Parliament, opposition leaders across parties continued to seek answers from Shah and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The issue contributed to repeated disruptions.The government, meanwhile, maintained that Shah was ready to discuss the student protests.In the final week of the session, Shah offered to address the opposition’s concerns directly.He offered to sit in Parliament from “3pm till 3pm the next day” to hear the opposition and respond to its points. Rahul rejected the offer, saying they “seek answers, not lectures”.Shah’s offer came amid demands that he make a statement in Parliament on the police action during the July 20 march over the NEET paper leak.He later wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla seeking time for a discussion on the student protest and NEET paper leak.“As you are aware, Hon’ble parliamentary affairs minister Shri Kiren Rijiju has agreed, on behalf of the government, to a discussion in Parliament on the student movement concerning the NEET examination, during the meeting of the Business Advisory Committee,” Shah said.He also pointed out that the Lok Sabha had already discussed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill during the session, but opposition MPs had not raised the NEET examination issue during that debate.The exchange captured the central political tension of the session.The government pointed to its legislative response and willingness to debate. The opposition demanded direct answers over the handling of the protests and accountability for the police action.The argument was therefore no longer simply about an examination paper leak. It had become a contest over responsibility, policing and ministerial accountability, much of it fought outside the chamber.Examination irregularities also became a political issue in Jharkhand, where the Centre’s political opponents were in power.Students in the state protested over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, including JPSC and JSSC, under the Hemant Soren government.In Ranchi, protesters marched towards the state assembly in an “assembly gherao”. The Soren government said it was open to talks and held rounds of discussions with student delegations.For the BJP at the Centre, the Jharkhand protests provided an opportunity to counter Rahul Gandhi’s attacks over the student movement in Delhi.Pradhan, days after resigning as education minister, turned his fire on Rahul.“The leader of opposition, who habitually lies, neither wants to come to Parliament nor listen to answers. They just want to spread their lies and shed crocodile tears,” Pradhan said.He also accused Rahul of making “baseless, factless false accusations” against Shah.The political irony was clear: the examination issue that had put the Union government under pressure in Delhi was now being used by the BJP to target the Congress, which is part of the ruling alliance with the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha government led by Hemant Soren.The student protests showed how street mobilisation could shape parliamentary politics. Another demonstration showed how the Parliament complex itself could become a stage for political messaging.The alleged theft of donations at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya became another opposition issue during the session.On Friday, Independent MP Pappu Yadav, along with other opposition MPs, staged a symbolic protest at Makar Dwar over the alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple donations. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party MPs Awadhesh Prasad and Dharmendra Yadav, and Jharkhand Mukti Morcha MP Mahua Maji participated.The MPs held placards and a large banner reading “Amit Shah Sadan Se Gayab Kyun?” They also raised slogans demanding Shah’s resignation and his presence in the House.Pappu Yadav, whose real name is Rajesh Ranjan, dressed as a temple priest carrying a photograph of Lord Ram and sat beside donation boxes. Opposition MPs acted as devotees and placed money in the box. Yadav then symbolically slipped the money into his pocket, representing the opposition’s allegation of theft.Videos circulating online also showed Rahul Gandhi putting money into the donation box. Another MP, playing a devotee, confronted the “priest” over the alleged act.The priest denied wrongdoing before theatrically leaving the scene. The INDIA bloc said the demonstration was intended to highlight the alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple donations and demand accountability from the Centre.It was a symbolic protest, but it reflected the broader character of the session: political messaging increasingly spilled into the physical spaces around Parliament.The Monsoon Session cannot simply be described as one in which Parliament failed to function. Bills were introduced and passed, financial business was completed, ordinances were replaced and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill became law.But the productivity figures tell another story. Lok Sabha functioned for approximately 19% of its scheduled time, while Rajya Sabha functioned for around 39%.Inside the Houses, protests and sloganeering repeatedly led to adjournments. Key government Bills were passed, often through voice votes. Outside, meanwhile, Parliament’s premises became venues for demonstrations and political performances.That contrast defined the session.The Jantar Mantar protest became a parliamentary issue. The police action turned into a political battle over Amit Shah. Pradhan’s resignation followed sustained pressure over the examination controversy. The same issue travelled to Jharkhand, where it became another weapon in the Centre’s political contest with the opposition. The Ram Mandir controversy then produced a symbolic demonstration inside the Parliament complex.In each case, the politics extended beyond the floor of the House.The Monsoon Session thus offered an unusual picture of parliamentary politics: legislation continued inside, while confrontation, mobilisation and political messaging increasingly took place outside. The Houses passed 12 Bills, but some of the session’s most visible battles were fought through protests, slogans, press statements, letters and demonstrations.Parliament was still working. But it was talking less, while the political argument increasingly moved beyond its walls.On August 13, both Houses adjourned sine die and will meet again in the Winter Session.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha functioned for 19% of its scheduled time, Rajya Sabha for around 39%. Question Hour was particularly badly hit, with less than 1% utilised. 12 Bills were passed by Lok Sabha and 12 by Rajya, with 12 Bills cleared by both Houses during the session.

Article Title: Jharkhand students stir: Govt makes fresh peace bid, invites protesters for talks on Aug 17
Article Text:
The latest invitation comes after six rounds of discussions between the Jharkhand government and the protesting students failed to produce a settlement.

Six rounds of talks held earlier

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand government has invited students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations for a fresh round of talks on Monday, August 17, in an attempt to resolve the 23-day-old standoff over demands for a CBI probe and cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination.The talks are scheduled for 2 pm at the State Guest House, with the government also allowing the students to participate alongside their legal advisor, an official said on Sunday.The decision followed a meeting between the Sub-Divisional Officer and the ADM, Law and Order, and protesting students at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where the agitation is being held.“The protesters have been invited for talks on August 17 at 2 pm. The students have been offered the proposal to participate in the discussions along with their legal advisor,” the official said.The ‘JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch’, which is spearheading the agitation, said it had accepted the government's invitation and would attend the meeting, but stressed that its core demands remained unchanged.“We will definitely go for the talks as we want to resolve the issue through dialogue.But, we are firm on two demands – a CBI probe into irregularities in recruitment tests and cancellation of the JSSC-CGL (Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission-Combine Graduate Level) exams,” Manch leader Ravindra Paswan told reporters.Paswan said the talks would be held in the presence of the students' legal advisor. The number of students who will form the delegation to meet the government panel will be announced on Monday.The latest invitation comes after six rounds of discussions between the Jharkhand government and the protesting students failed to produce a settlement.The previous round of talks, held on August 9, ended without any breakthrough.The students have been demanding a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission.They are also seeking cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, one of the key points of contention between the protesters and the state government.The agitation had entered its 23rd day on Sunday, with the students continuing their protest at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.The fresh talks on Monday will therefore be the latest attempt by the government to break the deadlock, with the protesters signalling that they are willing to engage in dialogue but will continue to press for their two principal demands.
Article Summary: The latest invitation comes after six rounds of discussions between the Jharkhand government and the protesting students failed to produce a settlement. The ‘JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch’, which is spearheading the agitation, said it had accepted the government's invitation and would attend the meeting.

How the killings took place

Article Title: 'Apologise': Bankim Chandra descendant writes to Sonia Gandhi over Vande Mataram 'insult'

NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP MLA Sumitro Chatterjee on Sunday demanded an unconditional apology from senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi for allegedly disrespecting Vande Mataram Chatterjee is a direct descendant of renowned poet Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, who wrote the national song.In his letter, Chatterjee described the alleged incident on August 15, as the country celebrated its 80th Independence Day, as "not merely unfortunate but a shameless repetition of a historical mistake."He stated that he was writing as an "ordinary citizen, a patriot and a direct descendant of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay," and expressed "deep pain, emptiness, and anger" over the episode.He termed Sonia Gandhi's alleged reluctance to fully recite "Vande Mataram" an "insult" to the sacrifices of martyrs such as Khudiram Bose.Chatterjee also cited the song's role in the freedom movement, including its recitation by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani at the 1905 Benares Congress session, its singing by Bal Gangadhar Tilak's supporters during his 1909 sedition trial, and its use as a rallying cry by nationalist students at Hyderabad's Osmania University in 1938 despite the Nizam's restrictions.He also referred to Rabindranath Tagore's rendition of the song at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress.Chatterjee further claimed that the Congress' so-called "dual policy" was not new, recalling that in 1937, the party had "bowed" to Mohammad Ali Jinnah's objections and truncated the song that October. He argued that the shadow of that "compromise" was visible again in the party's conduct.Asserting that Vande Mataram was not the property of any one political party but the country's collective memory, Bankim Chandra's eternal legacy and a sacred national symbol earned through the blood and sacrifice of martyrs, Chatterjee maintained that respecting the song was tantamount to respecting the history of India's freedom struggle.He warned that "history forgives no one" and that any leadership which fails to respect its own mantra of freedom would be pushed by history into "the darkness of oblivion."Chatterjee added that the incident had "deeply" hurt the sentiments of the people of West Bengal and appealed to Gandhi to introspect and tender an unconditional apology to all countrymen, particularly the people of West Bengal, without any conditions.The incident he referred to took place during Independence Day celebrations at the Congress party headquarters in Delhi. A video from the event went viral, with several BJP leaders and social media users alleging that there was "discomfort" and repeated attempts to stop the full version of Vande Mataram from being sung.The 80th Independence Day marked the first time since independence that the national song was played at the official August 15 celebrations at Delhi's Red Fort. Vande Mataram was played both before and after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's address to the nation from the ramparts of the iconic monument.
Article Summary: West Bengal BJP MLA Sumitro Chatterjee is a direct descendant of poet Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, who wrote the national song. He called Sonia Gandhi's alleged reluctance to fully recite "Vande Mataram" an "insult" to the sacrifices of martyrs.

NEW DELHI: Former Union minister and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram on Sunday hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his “dimagi naxal” remarks, saying he was “proud” to be described by the term.“I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!” Chidambaram said in a post on X, a day after PM Modi, in his 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort, warned that although armed Naxalism was nearing its end, people with an ideological Naxal mindset continued to pose a threat.PM Modi had urged people to “identify and isolate” such individuals, saying they were looking for opportunities to promote violence and unrest and “drag the country on the wrong path”.The Prime Minister said his government had made ending Naxalism a priority after coming to power in 2014. He said decades of Maoist violence had destroyed the lives and aspirations of young people and claimed that more than 3,500 security personnel had been killed in the conflict.“Naxalism, Maoism destroyed the dreams of lakhs of youth. It stole the sons of numerous mothers, crushed the dreams of numerous mothers,” PM Modi said in his Independence Day address.He also alleged that people with a Maoist mindset had earlier occupied positions of influence in government committees and policymaking.“For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life, even in government committees this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives,” PM Modi said, before calling for the “dimagi naxal” to be identified and isolated.Chidambaram's response came a day after Congress had already attacked PM Modi over the remarks.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the Prime Minister of reviving the “urban naxal” label to target political opponents. He argued that the government had previously used the term despite Union home minister Amit Shah clarifying in Parliament that there was no official definition of “urban Naxal”.Ramesh also alleged that the government eventually adopted some of the issues raised by people it had labelled “urban Naxals”. He cited the caste census as an example, saying the idea had earlier been dismissed as reflecting “urban Naxal” thinking before the government announced a caste-based census.“First, you make derogatory remarks--calling them 'Urban Naxals' or 'Mental Naxals'--but later, you accept the very demands your political opponents were making,” Ramesh said, according to news agency ANI.The Congress leader had also earlier called PM Modi a “master abuser” in “Entire Political Science” while reacting to his use of the “urban naxal” and “dimagi naxal” labels.The broader opposition has also criticised PM Modi's remarks. CPI(M) general secretary M A Baby said his party opposed Naxalism but accused the government of using the “Naxal mentality” label to target political opponents.CPI general secretary D Raja described “dimagi naxal” as an attempt to stigmatise dissent.TMC leader Saket Gokhale similarly accused PM Modi of using the Independence Day platform to take “cheap shots” at his critics.PM Modi's remarks came as he declared that the government had made substantial progress in tackling armed Naxalism.He said Naxalism had kept large parts of the country and its population “hostage” for decades and had resulted in the deaths of thousands of security personnel.“In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing,” PM Modi said.At the same time, he cautioned that the end of armed insurgency did not mean the ideological challenge had disappeared.“Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path,” PM Modi said.He linked the issue to his broader call for young people to contribute to the government's vision of a developed India by 2047, arguing that remote areas once affected by Naxal violence were now seeing development.

NEW DELHI: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi’s iconic Red Fort to Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), according to the 38th report of its Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team.The attack on November 10 last year claimed 11 lives."Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS, not listed) continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity; it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised, small, scattered cells instead of large units. The attack in November 2025 on the Red Fort in Delhi was officially attributed to AQIS," the report, published on August 10, stated.The assessment marks a significant shift in the attribution of the Red Fort attack, which had earlier been linked to the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM).The report noted that one member state had attributed a series of attacks to JeM and also linked the group to the Red Fort blast.The explosion occurred around 7 pm when a moving Hyundai i20 erupted in flames near the iconic monument.Investigators identified Umar-e-Nabi as the driver of the car and suspect him of carrying out the attack as a suicide bomber.Read also: Red Fort blast: 7,500-page NIA charge sheet alleges ‘Operation Heavenly Hind’ to overthrow govt Launched in 2014, AQIS is a regional affiliate of Al-Qaida.The group was formed to expand the organisation’s activities across South Asia, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and parts of Afghanistan.Meanwhile, the latest UNSC assessment also flagged broader concerns over the activities and capabilities of Al-Qaida and Islamic State (ISIL/Da’esh) affiliates.The report noted that Al-Qaida and ISIL had for years shown interest in developing chemical and biological weapons but had so far failed to overcome the technical challenges involved. It also highlighted the widespread circulation of instructions on producing such agents in online terrorist communities.The report cited material published by ISIL’s English-language Invade magazine in February that included instructions related to botulinum toxin and cyanide. It also noted that ISIL-K had shown particular interest in ricin and circulated instructions on developing the toxin over the previous 12 months.
